raw_response:
My land is 19.1 mu total. I've been doing this for 15 years, so I know what works here in Quzhou. The wheat and maize grow on the same plots — I harvest the wheat in June and go straight into maize on the same ground. That's just how it's done here. Cotton is on a separate block. I keep about 13 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and about 6 mu in cotton. Cotton pays better per mu but it wears me out — especially at picking time when I'm shorthanded because my husband and brother-in-law are in the city. So I don't push the cotton area larger than I can handle alone with my mother-in-law.

For seeds, I buy whatever Jimai wheat variety the township supply cooperative has this year — last few years it's been Jimai 22 or similar, and my yields have been fine. Maize I always use hybrid — Zhengdan 958 mostly, because everyone nearby uses it and I can ask neighbors if something goes wrong. For cotton I buy the improved BT seeds from the county seed shop. They cost more but I spray less, which matters when I'm busy.

Fertilizer I do what my neighbors do. I put down compound fertilizer before sowing then top-dress urea at key stages. I know some people say we over-apply nitrogen here but I'd rather be safe — a bad harvest with 8 people in the house is not something I can afford. Irrigation comes from our well. Wheat needs more waterings, especially in spring when it's dry. Maize I can get away with fewer waterings if rain comes. Cotton I watch carefully at bolling time.

For tillage: after maize harvest I use the rotary tiller to prepare for wheat. When I go from wheat to maize I just direct-seed — no time for tillage in that window. For cotton beds I rotary till in spring.
